newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU may take U.S. to WTO in poultry dispute.
newsitem.headline: EU may take U.S. to WTO in poultry dispute.

text.p: The European Union may take the U.S. to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) because of its plans to block imports of EU poultry in a row over hygiene rules, Commission chief spokesman Nicholas van der Pas said on Friday.

"We have to wait (and see) exactly what they are," Van der Pas told a news briefing. "We do not rule the possibility to go to the WTO because we think that such measures on the basis of the announcements would indeed be unjustified."

On Wednesday, the chief U.S. negotiator Paul Drazek said that up to $1.0 million worth of imports of European poultry products would be blocked. The EU on April 1 imposed curbs on imports of $50 million of U.S. poultry.
The poultry row marred an agreement between the EU and U.S. over meat import rules.

In a statement, EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said the agreement marked an important step in boosting trade in red meat but regretted that the U.S. rejected Brussels' offer of a temporary solution over poultry.
Instead the U.S. was planning unjustified and unfair action against the EU poultry industry even though it was committed to respecting U.S. sanitary measures, he said.
"The U.S. action would be clearly in breach of its WTO sanitary and phytosanitary measures (SPS) obligations, and the EC would have to consider the appropriate action to be taken," Fischler added.
